speaker: Doctor
text: I am Dr. Agent. I understand you are experiencing sudden-onset vertigo; to begin my assessment, have you had any recent head trauma or episodes of hearing loss in one ear?

speaker: Patient
text: 59-year-old male. The patient presents to the emergency department with a sudden-onset sensation that the room is spinning, leading to several episodes of nausea and vomiting. The symptoms started as he was going to bed and lasted for approximately 3 minutes. He mentions that he has never experienced anything like this before and currently feels at his baseline.

speaker: Doctor
text: Thank you for the details; the fact that your vertigo lasted only about three minutes and has completely resolved is very helpful. To narrow this down, are you aware of any recent viral illnesses, high blood pressure, or does the sensation of spinning ever occur when you turn your head quickly?

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Sudden-onset sensation of the room spinning. I also have Nausea, Vomiting, Dizziness.

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Benign Paroxysmal Positional Vertigo (BPPV). The clinical picture of sudden, brief (3 minutes), spontaneous vertigo with nausea/vomiting that has now resolved is classic for BPPV. I recommend a Dix-Hallpike maneuver to confirm the diagnosis.
